text: Neural cue reactivity is increasingly being investigated as a biomarker of treatment response and relapse prediction in addiction disorders. While aberrant brain responses to salient cues (e.g., drugs) have been widely reported in addiction, it is unclear whether these brain responses persist during longer-term abstinence and how they compare between substance use disorder and obesity and relate to potential differences in eating behaviors. As part of the Gut Hormones in ADDiction (GHADD) neuroimaging study, we investigated how salient cue reactivity to drugs or food, craving and eating behaviors compare in three clinical populations where alterations have been previously observed: abstinent nicotine use disorder (NUD), alcohol use disorder (AUD), and obesity.
source_label: Salient cue reactivity and eating behaviors in ex-smokers, abstinent alcohol use disorder, and obesity
